```kotlin
data class Exercise(

}
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of cross‑process isolation, secure data handling, and Android background work constraints in a real-world telemetry scenario.

## Key Concepts
- Cross‑process IPC with AIDL in a sandboxed collector
- Encrypted local storage (Room + Android Keystore)
- WorkManager constraints (Wi‑Fi, charging, backoff)
- Data minimization and user opt-out
- Testing IPC boundaries, memory budgets, and data leakage risks

## Code Example

```javascript
class TelemetryEvent {
  constructor(type, ts, userHash, payload) {
    this.type = type
    this.ts = ts
    this.userHash = userHash
    this.payload = payload
  }
}
function enqueueEvent(event) { /* host -> collector IPC */ }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you verify no data leaks across the process boundary?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This checks practical Android networking, simple architecture, and lifecycle safety for beginners.

## Key Concepts
- Retrofit service and data model
- Repository pattern with in-memory cache
- Kotlin coroutines with retry/backoff
- ViewModel and LiveData for UI state
- Basic test plan coverage

## Code Example
```kotlin
data class Post(val userId: Int, val id: Int, val title: String, val body: String)
interface PostsApi { suspend fun getPosts(): List<Post> }
class PostsRepository(private val api: PostsApi) {
  private var cache: List<Post>? = null
  suspend fun getPosts(): List<Post> {
    cache?.let { return it }
    val data = api.getPosts()
    cache = data
    return data
  }
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test network failures and backoff behavior?
- How would you ensure cancellation and avoid leaks in ViewModel?
